why: Seller signals are public, the fund owns the overlap data, and a backtest on real reported pension sales can show lead time.
decided: Target fund is assumed to buy LP-led secondaries.
Optimise for a data leader audience over an engineering audience.
Public data allowed on the seller side; buyer portfolio synthetic; real seller names anonymised before publishing (CLAUDE.md amended).
The system drafts outreach; a human sends. No agent contacts or negotiates with a seller.
Streaming is a learning spike; batch ships unless measured otherwise.
Real buyer organisations stay out of all outputs.
Both gates in scope: First Call (Gate 0) and Quick Look (Gate 1).
Plain-language wording for readers outside private capital.
Rough value assessment: about $4.36M per year (Quick Look $0.29M, First Call $3.98M), all inputs assumed.
Quick Look matching reports depth in three tiers, not a known/unknown flag: same fund (we get its reports), same manager but another fund, unknown. Carry into the PRD.
Every verdict (First Call: call now or wait; Quick Look: look closer or pass) opens into a confidence level and reasons, each tied to a rule and a number.
The team supplies its own plain-text rulebook (a skill-style blueprint) for what a good deal is; the AI applies it, not its own judgement.
Analysts can override any verdict with a one-line reason; overrides are stored as a record for improving rules and AI. Problem 4 added: verdicts kept without override 80% or more.
First Call promises preparation (PREPARE / WATCH), not exclusive direct deals.
Value shown as low/base/high net of cost; First Call is an option with a 0.1% break-even.
Quick Look identifies funds by ratio fingerprint (% called, DPI, TVPI, value/commitment), not names.
